results.note: Recorded (Musicaphon, 'Trio for Violin and Horn in D major', 3 mvts, 10:15), but the Lund MS says only 'Sigr. Graun'; IMSLP says it may be Johann Gottlieb or Carl Heinrich; Apple credits the movements to both brothers. Keep, with the doubt in notes.

Exists and is recorded (Concert Royal Koeln, Musicaphon 2009, 4 mvts Adagio-Allegro-Largo-Menuet, 9:31, credited to C.H. Graun). But the source scores the bass only as 'Basso' (IMSLP tags bassoon, cello or continuo); the same disc's E-major sister piece is billed for oboe d'amore, horn and bassoon, so no string part is shown and 'cello' is the researcher's guess. Scope needs a string instrument: either reject as out of scope or rescore the bass as continuo.

Weak on three counts. (1) The Lund MS (No. 6) is anonymous (corno.de lists it as 'Anonymous'); the Graun attribution is IMSLP's, and the number 'GraunWV Cv:SV:106' appears only on that page (possibly a typo for Cv:XV:106), so it cannot be confirmed. (2) Same bass/scope doubt as Lund 7 ('Basso', no string part shown). (3) Recording match unsure: the Musicaphon disc has an E-flat 'Concerto' (3 mvts) and an E-major 'Trio for oboe d'amore, horn and bassoon' (3 mvts Allegro-Largo-Allegro, credited partly to J.G. Graun); IMSLP's Lund MS has 4 mvts.

note: Gubaidulina: all 14 are recorded and in scope; where Sikorski's durations differ from the recordings (Piano Quintet 20' vs ~30; Hommage 40' vs 33; SQ3 15' vs 18) the recording timings were kept. Gyrowetz Op. 29 vs IMSLP's Op. 42: the catalogue's separate Op. 42 Nos. 1-3 (F, D, C minor) are Gombart's different set, so no duplicate. Graun Lund 7 and Cv:SV:106 may fail the string-instrument rule.
